sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force October 31, 2012) including investment chapter
Panama–Netherlands Income and Capital Tax Treaty (signed 2000)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of April 27, 2015 (AML/CFT), as amended by Law No. 70 of 2019; Executive Decree No. 363 of May 27, 2015, as amended; Law No. 52 of 2016 establishing the beneficial owner registry; Law No. 70 of 2019 introducing mandatory UBO sworn declarations for legal entities; Law No. 25 of June 12, 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; directives of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and implementing resolutions of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority of the founder's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or issuing financial institution in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where certified form is required by the Panamanian resident agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank or credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document; notarization and apostille required if mandated by the resident agent's KYC/AML policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents and certificate of good standing of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague Convention registries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the corporate founder authorizing incorporation of the Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous screening of each founder, council member, protector and identified ultimate beneficial owner against OFAC SDN/Consolidated lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU financial sanctions lists, and Panama's national sanctions and frozen-asset directives issued by the UAF. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, including senior-management approval and source-of-wealth documentation, in accordance with Law No. 23 of 2015. Screening results, risk ratings and supporting documents must be archived for no less than five (5) years following termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Services Portal, 'Reserva de Nombre' module (www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be written in Latin script; Spanish and Latin-script foreign languages are accepted. Names originating in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Spanish or English Latin characters. The name must include the statutory designation 'Fundación de Interés Privado', 'Private Interest Foundation', or the abbreviations 'F.I.P.' / 'P.I.F.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any token implying regulated financial, medical, legal or educational activity without the corresponding ministerial or supervisory license
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name reservation may be challenged by filing a 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification. If denied, a second-instance 'recurso de apelación' may be lodged with the corresponding administrative superior, with ultimate judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Supreme Court of Panama. A valid name certificate may be extended once for an additional thirty (30) days upon written request and payment of the renewal fee prior to expiry, subject to a fresh availability check and re-screening of founders against sanctions lists.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as a non-statutory operational address. The foundation must at all times maintain a physical registered office in Panama through a licensed resident agent, who stocks legal documents, receives service of process, and holds the AML/UBO file. A purely digital EdTech subscription business hosted outside Panama does not require local employees or physical office premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection of the foundation's premises is approximately one to three percent (1-3%) for a Low_Risk_Standard EdTech structure without local operations. Regulatory attention focuses instead on the resident agent's client files, which are subject to documentary reviews and periodic compliance inspections by UAF-supervised authorities and the Registro Público.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent / law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for a low-risk, non-complex foundation structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard low-risk retail subscription business

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations) as amended by Ley 35 de 1996; Articles 18, 19 and 32.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter) and Estatutos (Regulations) submitted as Notarial Testimonio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial patrimony of US$10,000 or its equivalent in admissible assets; must be subscribed and evidenced to the notary; no statutory escrow or custodial deposit requirement is imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], PANAMA. 1. The Founder's contributed capital of US$10,000 is hereby accepted as the initial patrimony. 2. The registered office of the Foundation is established at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama. 3. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer, each with sole and joint authority as conferred by the Charter. 4. The Foundation and its officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and take all lawful acts to implement the EdTech language-learning business. 5. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct corporate counsel to prepare the Acta Constitutiva and Estatutos in Spanish, including founder identification, initial patrimony of US$10,000, purpose relating to ISIC 6201 interactive language education, registered office address, governance rules, and appointment of officers and protector (if any).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder's passport or ID
Bank certificate or asset valuation evidencing US$10,000 patrimony
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel detects substantive defects, the drafts are revised and resubmitted within 5 business days without additional registry charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Foundation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founder or authorized attorney executes the Foundation Charter before the notary. The notary shall authenticate the signatures, verify the initial patrimony evidence, and issue a certified notarial testimonio containing the full text of the instrument and its annexes.
required_dossiers: Against such instrument endorsed by legal counsel
Evidence of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses due to defective patrimony evidence, obtain corrected bank confirmation or sworn statement of asset valuation and re-submit within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Fundaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial testimonio and an application for inscription of the Private Interest Foundation. Pay the statutory registration fee of US$250. The registry will examine legal compliance, assign a filing number, and issue a certificate of inscribed foundation (Personería Jurídica).
required_dossiers: Notarial testimonio of the Foundation Charter
Legalized copy of the notary's certification
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice (nota de objeción), cure the referred issues within 15 business days by filing an amended charter or supplementation document; failure to cure voids the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the registered foundation certificate, apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) and obtain an Aviso de Inscripción de Fundación para efectos fiscales. This step activates tax filing obligations and enables opening of corporate bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requires additional documentation, provide corrected apostilled or consularized copies within 10 business days; expedite through the DGI 'Sede Principal' taxpayer assistance desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Deposit Fulfillment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian Bank of the foundation's choosing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the registered foundation documentation and supporting RUC to open a corporate bank account. This step is necessary for the EdTech subscription payment rails (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing). Complete Know Your Customer (KYC) diligence and deposit operational capital in accordance with the foundation's purpose.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership details, submit a sworn declaration and internal governance chart; if rejected, approach an alternate licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional Municipal Business Permit for Physical Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá - Dirección de Avisos de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a physical office or administrative center is established in Panama City, file an Aviso de Operación with the municipality. This permit covers non-industrial commercial activities, including software development and online tutoring services.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires zoning verification, obtain the landlord's zoning certificate and resubmit within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - no industrial license required for ISIC 6201 software and e-learning services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating permit; optional 'Aviso de Operación' from Municipio de Panamá only when a physical office is opened

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MIAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ISIC 6201 digital service provider with only office-based operations; no formal EIA report or environmental registration requirement is triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge in normal software operations; if offices generate e-waste, comply with Panama's General Environmental Law (Ley 41 de 1998) and municipal solid waste ordinances; non-hazardous office waste must be segregated and collected by licensed waste operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical office, complete Fire Safety Inspection Certification from Dirección General de Bomberos (DGB) verifying extinguishers, exits and electrical safety; structural load inspection for office signage, and occupational workplace clearance from Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) covering sanitary conditions, restrooms and employee safety per current workplace regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), an organ of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of Panama; digital filing via Sede Electrónica de la DGI and the RUC/ITBMS portal (dgi.mef.gob.pa; sede.mef.gob.pa). Customs matters are administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the SIGA customs system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in taxable business must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) before commencing activities. The applicant files the constitutional document (Foundation Charter registered in the Registro Público, or certified foreign incorporation documents with translation/legalization), designates a resident legal representative or fiscal agent, registers the commercial and business address, and obtains Municipal Aviso de Operación where applicable. Non-resident digital service suppliers that derive ITBMS-liable revenue from Panama customers must complete remote RUC registration through a Panamanian fiscal agent; no minimum capital or local equity is required for foreign-owned PIFs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections in the US/CFC sense. A PIF may, by its charter or founder's instructions, elect to act either as a non-commercial patrimonial foundation (ordinarily not engaged in taxable commercial transactions) or as a commercial foundation, becoming a corporate taxpayer on Panama-source business income only. The territorial system is mandatory and does not permit a worldwide-income election or pass-through/transparent treatment for income tax purposes; branch remittance and dividend withholding rules apply only when profits are distributed from Panama-source funds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-equivalent tax imposed by Código Fiscal, including the specific digital services provisions for cross-border online education and downloadable software.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general numeric de minimis for ITBMS registration: RUC registration is mandatory for any person performing taxable transfers of goods or services, including software subscriptions and e-commerce, unless covered by the small-taxpayer simplified regime for businesses with annual gross income up to PAB 36,000 (US$ 36,000). Non-resident digital service providers must register and collect ITBMS when they supply services to consumers resident or located in Panama, regardless of total global turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has phased in mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) administered by DGI. Commercial software or DGI's free electronic invoice tool must render invoices in XML/DGI format, obtain digital validation from the DGI authorization queue before the sale may be fiscally delivered, assign a fiscally valid sequential stamp/correlation, and transmit the invoice and credit/debit notes in real time. The DGI may block billing numbers and apply fines for pre-validation billing; paper invoices are permissible only in the authorized imprenta-virtual transitional regime for certain small taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% ITBMS) applies to the export of goods and to services provided to non-resident customers for use or consumption entirely outside Panama, including online language-learning subscriptions and automated tutoring software supplied abroad by a Panamanian PIF, provided the service is not effectively connected to Panama, payment is received from abroad in freely convertible currency, and the subscription contract, terms of use, user geolocation data, and server/delivery records evidence foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SIGA electronic customs export declaration (Declaración Aduanera de Exportación)
Commercial invoice and signed subscription/licence agreement with the foreign customer

Transport document: Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for goods; for SaaS and digital services, the certified digital delivery log, IP/geolocation record, and platform in-app purchase reconciliation report
Inward remittance certificate or bank settlement statements evidencing foreign-source cash inflow (including Apple IAP and Google Play proceeds-net-of-commission statements)
DGI export registration and, where applicable, the export licence or free-sale certificate required by the destination market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit review compares invoice flows, platform settlement reports, and customs records to verify the reality of foreign consumption; false zero-rating is recharacterized as taxable domestic service revenue, attracting 7% ITBMS, default interest, and fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the omitted tax under Código Fiscal sanctions, plus possible criminal prosecution for tax fraud and money laundering where the alleged sham export is used to launder funds; export privileges and RUC validity may be suspended pending resolution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama operates without a central bank and without any monetary or exchange-control authority. Banking supervision is conducted by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decree Law 2 of 1971 and Decree Law 9 of 1998; monetary statistics and balance-of-payments coordination are handled by the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the U.S. Dollar is legal tender, and the Balboa is a purely nominal accounting unit pegged 1:1 to the USD. There is no national currency and therefore no capital-account vs current-account convertibility distinction; all transactions may be freely settled in USD, EUR, or any convertible currency. Profit remittance is unrestricted: dividends, royalties, and service fees require no exchange approval. Withholding taxes apply only on Panamanian-source income (notably the 5% dividend withholding on distributions), and beneficial-ownership transparency obligations apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export-proceeds surrender requirement. EdTech subscription revenue and export receipts may be retained or disbursed freely in USD without central-bank clearance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low. Panama does not maintain an EU-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime. Electronic-money issuance and payment processing are confined to SBP-licensed banks and supervised payment providers under the SBP regulatory perimeter, including Acuerdo 5-2018 on payment systems and the Ley 697 de 2023 framework for financial innovation. Offshore digital EMIs can only operate as white-label payment facilitators and require a Panamanian correspondent bank or a local licensed bank account to deliver final USD settlement for a PIF; they are suitable as treasury plumbing, not as a primary custodian.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the Founder, at least one Foundation Council member, or a properly authorized signatory is generally mandatory for first-time corporate account opening at Tier-1 Panamanian banks, especially for a Private Interest Foundation with nominee organs. Remote opening is occasionally available for existing clients of the bank, but for a new PIF the standard SBP due-diligence expectation is an in-person interview at a Panama City branch or verification via a Panamanian consulate notarization combined with a bank officer video interview. Compliance committees normally treat this interview as non-waivable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Foundation (PIF) using nominee Council and an anonymous foundation beneficiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified excerpt from the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, foundation charter and foundation regulations, notarized declaration of the Founder and Beneficiary, apostilled passport pages, professional reference letters from the founding attorneys, and a bank reference letter from the originating institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance deficiency: PIF viewed as a shell without local management or operational activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantive file comprising Panama office lease, corporate services agreement with a licensed resident agent, local management engagement letters, Foundation Council meeting minutes, and annual financial statements reflecting actual subscription revenue and operating expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for EdTech collections disbursed through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Payout Reports, Google Payment Center settlement statements, Stripe or other payment processor payout logs, subscriber volume reports, marketing and vendor invoices, and audited management accounts reconciling net platform proceeds to bank inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or adverse-media flag on the Founder or Council members.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed compliance questionnaire, professional curricula vitae, references from regulated Panamanian lawyers or accountants, adverse-media search report from an approved screening provider, and a narrative memorandum explaining transaction purpose and fund provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented inbound funding: repeated small card-payout tranches perceived as possible structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed settlement agreements with Apple and Google, merchant account breakdown by country, intercompany reconciliation of subscription revenue, audited financial statements, and a 12-month treasury cash-flow projection letter from the appointed financial advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be routed as SWIFT USD transfers through the correspondent banking network into the PIF's USD-denominated operational or escrow account. Field 50K (Ordering Customer) must show the Founder or subscribing investor; field 59 (Beneficiary) must identify the PA_PIF entity and account; field 56/57 must show a U.S. clearing correspondent such as JPMorgan Chase New York or BNY Mellon where required; field 70 must state a precise purpose, e.g., 'Capital Subscription' or 'Foundation Funding', and must not reference prohibited activities. The receiving Panamanian bank will require the foundation registry number, RUC, certified beneficial-ownership excerpt, and source-of-funds documentation. Because Panama is dollarized, no FX conversion or central-bank declaration is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements execute primarily through SWIFT MT103 messages for vendor payments, royalty distributions, and service invoices; for higher-value or condition-based payments, Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) advised through a Panamanian bank provide secured settlement. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing disbursements are received by the PIF as periodic aggregated net settlement vouchers remitted by Apple and Google treasury partners directly to the operational account; onward intercompany transfers are made by MT103 referencing invoices, W-8BEN-E certificates, and economic-substance memoranda. No Panamanian central-bank approval is required; only bank-level sanctions screening (including OFAC and UN lists) and liquidity limits apply.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forwards in EUR/USD and GBP/USD for non-USD subscription revenue, executed through Panamanian licensed banks or U.S. prime brokers under ISDA/CSA documentation
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies such as BRL, MXN, and COP, booked offshore with a licensed international counterparty to economically hedge subscriber exposure
Cross-currency swaps (ISDA Master Agreement) converting EUR or GBP revenue streams into USD while aligning with Apple and Google settlement cycles
Multi-currency deposit accounts and USD cash sweep facilities at Tier-1 Panamanian banks to reduce conversion friction
Zero-cost collar option strategies for large single-currency receivables, subject to counterparty bespoke-risk approval

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial tax system: Panama-source income is taxed at 25%; qualifying foreign-source income is generally exempt. No general statutory tax holiday applies to EdTech subscription income, although the SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime may provide a reduced effective rate for qualifying regional headquarters activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form DGI-02 (Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through Panama's Sede Electrónica de la DGI (e-Tax portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within three months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from all sources attributable to Panama (territorial source).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF must report only Panama-source income; foreign-source EdTech subscription revenue is excluded when sourced abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income specifically exempt under Panamanian law or income sourced outside Panama under territorial rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentation supporting foreign-source classification must be retained, including subscriber location records and IP hosting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses deductible against Panama-source gross income, subject to arm's length and territorial apportionment rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses connected to foreign-source income are not deductible against Panama-source income; proper allocation is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross taxable Panama-source income minus allowable deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source activity exists, net taxable income is zero; a loss may be declared and carried forward for five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the statutory 25% rate on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if no Panama-source taxable income; no minimum tax is imposed for inactive EdTech foundations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, plus monthly surcharges of 1.5% per month (capped at 30 months); failure to file a nil return can trigger administrative fines up to USD 1,000. Interest accrues on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or distributions paid out of Panama-source taxable profits; distributions of already-taxed profits or foreign-source income may be exempt if documentary evidence is maintained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the DGI, complete and file the applicable treaty relief form, and submit the TRC to the withholding agent before the payment date. The withholding agent must attach the TRC and treaty position to the withholding tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 12.5% on interest paid to non-residents and 12.5% on royalties paid for the use of IP/technical services. Treaty rates may be reduced under Panama's limited DTA network (e.g., Mexico, Spain, UAE, Qatar, Luxembourg, Barbados, among others); specific treaty eligibility must be verified on a case-by-case basis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File documentation is required for multinational groups with Panama operations when annual transactions with related parties exceed USD 10 million, or when tangible/intangible transactions exceed USD 250,000 per related party. Panamanian entities with annual turnover above USD 10 million must also prepare transfer pricing documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities, including Private Interest Foundations, that earn relevant income from activities such as distribution, service, financing, or intellectual property. An EdTech PIF must demonstrate substantial economic activity in Panama for core income-generating activities (employees, premises, management) proportionate to its income; failure to comply triggers annual penalties and potential strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or false declaration of Panama-source EdTech subscription revenue on Form DGI-02, use of fictitious invoices, or concealment of taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment of the responsible parties; civil penalties include accrued interest, 50% surcharge on unpaid tax, and administrative sanctions from the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members who sign false returns can be jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, penalties, and surcharges; criminal conviction can lead to travel bans, civil restitution, and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Private Interest Foundation as a pure nominee without any actual office, staff, or business activity in Panama while claiming foreign-source exemption to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of income as Panama-source, retroactive taxation at 25% plus penalties, Economic Substance Regulation fines up to USD 250,000, possible foundation dissolution, and cancellation of the registered agent license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the foundation's tax liabilities under look-through principles; they face travel bans, director disqualification, and civil restitution for amounts unjustly avoided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transparent records of beneficial ownership, source of funds, or subscriber payment flows routed through high-risk jurisdictions without AML/KYC procedures under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, freezing of accounts, revocation of the foundation's legal status, and compulsory reporting to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and resident agents can be held criminally liable for money laundering if proceeds derive from tax fraud; applicable penalties include imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, travel bans, and personal forfeiture of assets.
